context: Write a threat model first, then use the SDK authentication interface with TLS termination at the deployment boundary. Validate Host and Origin with TransportSecuritySettings. Derive an authenticated principal/workspace context for every request and use it to scope results, charts, exports, and execution records. Add authorization, per-principal rate/cost/scale/platform quotas, global and per-principal concurrency admission, bounded queues, and structured audit events. Reuse existing path containment and secret-scrubbing behavior; use durable shared stores for multi-worker limits rather than process globals. Keep remote binding gated behind explicit secure configuration that fails closed.
description: The stdio subprocess boundary currently supplies implicit local trust. A remote HTTP endpoint would expose benchmark execution against configured databases plus result and chart file access. Stateless protocol requests do not provide authentication, authorization, tenant storage isolation, quotas, safe scheduling, or auditing. Build those controls before allowing any non-loopback bind or documenting a shared endpoint.

anti_patterns.dont: make 0.0.0.0 or :: the default bind address
anti_patterns.instead: default to loopback and require explicit secure remote configuration
anti_patterns.why: it turns an opt-in local feature into an exposed execution surface

anti_patterns.dont: treat stateless MCP as an authentication or authorization mechanism
anti_patterns.instead: authenticate every request and authorize every protected operation
anti_patterns.why: sessionless protocol transport does not establish identity or permissions

anti_patterns.dont: trust caller-supplied workspace or artifact paths
anti_patterns.instead: derive tenancy from the authenticated principal and resolve beneath server-owned roots
anti_patterns.why: that permits cross-tenant access and traversal

anti_patterns.dont: use process-local dictionaries or semaphores as authoritative multi-worker quotas
anti_patterns.instead: coordinate limits through a durable shared backend
anti_patterns.why: requests can alternate workers and processes restart

preserves.behavior: Existing result-path containment and MCP error secret scrubbing remain enforced
Local stdio clients require no remote authentication configuration and retain current behavior
No credential, bearer token, database DSN, or raw secret material is written to logs or audit records
Remote bind remains fail-closed until authentication and transport-security configuration are valid
